0.x: **Shrenis:** associations of artisans, merchants and moneylenders under elected or hereditary heads (**jetthaka / pamukha**). Craft shrenis trained workers, procured raw materials and sold products; merchant shrenis organised trade.

r: Fixed **wages, rules of work, standards and prices**; had **their own laws (shreni-dharma)** and **judicial powers** over members
Deposits invested at interest – the **Nashik inscription** records guild deposits at fixed interest
**Caravan / convoy of merchants**, or its leader

1.x: **Punch-marked (Aahat) coins:** the **earliest extant coins** of India (7th–6th c. BC to the Mauryan period); **mostly silver**, some copper; symbols only (**sun, animals, trees, hills**), no writing.
Called **panas / karshapanas**; issued under the Haryankas, Nandas and Mauryas; the first definite literary references are in **Pali texts**.

r: **Gold / a gold ornament** in Vedic texts (nishka-griva = gold necklace); a prestige object, later a unit
Standard silver or copper punch-marked coin
Value or weight unit of 100 mana

1.x: The **Satavahanas** first used inherited punch-marked coins, then die-struck coins of **lead**, potin, copper and silver; **ship-mast** coins of **Yajnasri Satakarni**.
**Vaishya Tekri** (near Ujjain): a Mauryan-era (BCE) stupa bigger than Sanchi; punch-marked and cast Avanti coins; MP to re-excavate it (2026).

r: Linked **Taxila** (north-west) with the Ganga valley up to Tamralipti
Southern route to the Deccan (Kaushambi–Ujjayini–Pratishthana), through **Assaka**

2.x: **Pali terms for settlements:** **nigama** = (market) town, **nagara** = large city; the Vedic **pur** = fortified settlement.

3.x: **NBPW:** fine, glossy black, mirror-like **deluxe tableware of the rich**; **c. 700–200 BCE**; **after Painted Grey Ware**; the hallmark of the second urbanisation.
**NBPW sites:** mainly the Ganga valley – Hastinapur, Kaushambi, Shravasti, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Rajgir, Pataliputra, Vaishali, Champa; also Ujjain, Vidisha, Taxila.

r: Forest clearance in the Ganga plain; surplus

3.x: **Over 60 towns** in 600–300 BCE; the Mahajanapadas and Magadha = the **second urbanisation**.
**Rajghat (Varanasi):** pre-NBPW levels, punch-marked coins, **Greek-inscribed seals**; a BHU re-study (Sep 2026) puts urban Varanasi at **c. 800 BCE**.

r: c. 2172 BCE; southern Iron Age c. 2100 BCE – older than the Gangetic Iron Age
